name: Noodle
description: Turns an architecture described as code into clear, presentation-grade diagrams.
why: Diagrams are **generated, not drawn**: the agent reads your code (Helm, Terraform, Kubernetes), writes the system as files, and Noodle draws it with official logos and ports. It **refuses to output a diagram** whose lines cross boxes or whose labels collide. Installs as a Claude Code plugin; PNG export needs draw.io.
yes: Explaining how a request travels through your platform
A tech stack or service catalogue for a slide
Keeping a diagram in sync with the code, reviewed in PRs
no: Drawings that are not about a system's architecture

examples.title: A request path
examples.input:
Draw how a user request reaches a tenant
app and what keeps tenants apart, with `noodle`.
examples.output: A topology diagram built from the code: each hop with its port, the login flow, and a **Gaps** card where the docs and the code disagree.

examples.title: A login sequence
examples.input:
Show the OIDC login steps of a user
without a session, with `noodle`.
examples.output: A sequence diagram that reuses the same model: every request and reply, in order.

examples.title: A tech stack
examples.input:
Give me our tech stack on one slide,
with `noodle`.
examples.output: A landscape view grouped by layer, with planned items marked as such.
